title: `exists_nowhereDense_spectralSet` asks for an example in every dimension `d ≥ 2`, not in some dimension
summary: `NowhereDenseSpectralSet.exists_nowhereDense_spectralSet` puts the `answer(sorry)` slot opposite `∀ d ≥ 2, ∃ Ω : Set (Fin d → ℝ)` bounded, measurable, nowhere dense, of positive measure and spectral, whereas KLM Problem 7.1 asks whether such an Ω exists at all in dimensions two and higher; because a product with a spectral cube carries an example from dimension d to every larger dimension, the Lean proposition is equivalent to the two-dimensional case rather than to the source's question.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5346 (merged pull request) adds a nonempty-interior hypothesis to `SpectralSetProduct.spectralProductImpliesRightSpectral` and a `NullMeasurableSet`/positive-measure requirement to `spectralPair`, which closed #5228; it does not touch `NowhereDenseSpectralSet.exists_nowhereDense_spectralSet`, so the dimension quantifier reported here is unaffected.

title: `GrowthCondition`'s real-valued `liminf` excludes sequences with `aₙ^(1/2ⁿ) → ∞`
summary: `Erdos1051.GrowthCondition` takes `Filter.liminf (fun n => ((a n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 ^ n : ℝ))) Filter.atTop > 1` in ℝ, where the liminf of an unbounded family is the supremum of its eventual lower bounds and hence defaults to 0, so the condition is false for sequences such as `a n = (n + 2) ^ (2 ^ n)` whose roots are `n + 2` and tend to +∞, and `erdos_1051` therefore omits the infinite-liminf case that Erdős–Graham and [BKKKZ26] explicitly include.

title: `erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity` fixes `answer(False)`, but [Th17] proves that statement true
summary: `Erdos1067.erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity` fixes `answer(False)` against the assertion that every graph of chromatic cardinal `ℵ₁` has an infinitely edge-connected subgraph of chromatic cardinal `ℵ₁`, and its docstring says Thomassen constructed a counterexample, whereas Thomassen's Theorem 2 in [Th17] proves precisely that statement (every graph of uncountable chromatic number has a subgraph of infinite edge-connectivity and uncountable chromatic number), so the answer should be `True`.

title: `FactorialSums` allows index 0, so 0! and 1! are counted separately and the set is too large
summary: `Erdos1108.FactorialSums` sums `n.factorial` over an arbitrary `Finset ℕ`, so a finset containing both 0 and 1 counts the value 1 twice and the set contains e.g. 4 = 0! + 1! + 2! and every n! + 4 with n ≥ 3, none of which is a sum of distinct positive-index factorials, whereas the source's sums ∑ εᵢ i! run over i ≥ 1 (Brindza–Erdős, eq. (2)), so both `erdos_1108.parts.i` and `erdos_1108.parts.ii` ask their finiteness questions about a strictly larger set A.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4354 (open pull request) touches this file, replacing the local `IsPowerful` definition with `Nat.Powerful` in `erdos_1108.parts.ii`; it does not change `FactorialSums`, whose index set stays an unrestricted `Finset ℕ`, so the defect reported here is untouched.

title: `variants.shparlinski` and `variants.glibichuk` bound the all-primes constant `C ε`, which is not polynomial in `ε⁻¹`
summary: `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.shparlinski` and `Erdos1180.erdos_1180.variants.glibichuk` assert `(C ε : ℝ) ≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 3` and `≤ K * ε⁻¹ ^ 2` for the file's `C ε`, the least summand bound valid for *all* primes, whereas Shparlinski's and Glibichuk's bounds are stated for primes above a threshold depending on ε; taking ε = log(3/2)/log p makes 1 the only admissible denominator, so `C ε ≥ p − 1` while the asserted bounds are only O((log p)^3) and O((log p)^2).

title: `janzer_even`, `cubic` and `janzer_conjecture` are trivial: the witness may be the empty graph
summary: The existentials in `erdos_147.variants.janzer_even`, `erdos_147.variants.cubic` and `erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture` ask for `(q : ℕ)` and `H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)` without requiring `0 < q`, and for `q = 0`, `H = ⊥` bipartiteness holds, `H.IsRegularOfDegree r` is vacuous and `extremalNumber n H = 0` for every `n`, so all three statements (including the whole right-hand side of `janzer_conjecture`'s `answer(sorry) ↔ …`) hold for any exponent without using the degree, parity or positivity hypotheses, whereas Janzer's constructions and conjecture concern nonempty regular graphs.

title: `erdos_189.variants.parallelogram` asserts `¬ Erdos189For …`, fixing a negative answer to an open question
summary: `Erdos189.erdos_189.variants.parallelogram` states `¬ Erdos189For …` outright, asserting that some finite colouring of ℝ² has no colour class containing parallelograms of every positive area, while Erdős–Graham, Kovač (arXiv:2309.09973) and erdosproblems.com/189 pose the parallelogram case as an open yes-or-no question and the declaration itself carries `category research open`; with no `answer(sorry)` slot the file commits to an unknown answer.

title: `erdos_308.variants.croot` bounds `f N` where Croot's theorem bounds `f N - 1`
summary: `Erdos308.erdos_308.variants.croot` places `f N`, defined in this file as the smallest non-representable positive integer, between the two floors of Croot's Main Theorem, but Croot bounds η(N), the largest integer up to which every integer is representable, which is `f N - 1`; since (log log N)²/log N → 0 the shift is not absorbed by the o(1) factors, and the stated upper bound eventually forces `f N ≤ m N`, contradicting Croot's lower bound, which gives `f N = m N + 1` for arbitrarily large N.

title: `variants.converse_implication` reverses the source's conditional between density 1 and Sidon-set embeddability
summary: `Erdos329.erdos_329.variants.converse_implication` states that `sSup {sidonUpperDensity A | IsSidon A} = 1` implies that every finite Sidon set embeds in a perfect difference set modulo some n > 0, the converse of the implication recorded on erdosproblems.com and in Erdős's 1980 survey (embeddability ⇒ density 1); since the consequent is false by the Alexeev–Mixon counterexample {1,2,4,8,13}, the declaration asserts that the supremum is *not* 1, contradicting the Erdős–Krückeberg conjecture the same file records.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4923 (open issue) lists Erdős 329 among statements whose unknown supremum can be copied into the `answer` slot so that the theorem closes by `rfl`; that concerns the main `erdos_329` statement, not the reversed implication in `erdos_329.variants.converse_implication` reported here.

title: `erdos_35.variants.plunnecke` omits Plünnecke's positive-density hypothesis and is false
summary: `erdos_35.variants.plunnecke` asserts `schnirelmannDensity A ^ (1 - (k : ℝ)⁻¹) ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B)` for every `A` with no lower bound on `schnirelmannDensity A`, so it fails at `B = Set.univ`, `k = 1`, `A = ∅`, where the exponent is 0, `Real.rpow` gives `0 ^ (0 : ℝ) = 1` and the sumset has Schnirelmann density 0 (and again at `A = Set.Ici 2`), whereas Plünnecke's Satz 1.2 assumes a density parameter in `(0, 1]`.

title: `erdos_361.asymptotic` is answered by `fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)` for every `c > 0`, so the Θ question is elementary
summary: `Erdos361.erdos_361.asymptotic` asks only for the `=Θ[atTop]` class of `fun n ↦ (subsetSumAvoidanceNumber c n : ℝ)`, which `answer(fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ))` satisfies for every `c > 0` (for an integer `k ≥ 1` with `1/k ≤ c`, the integers strictly between `n/(k+1)` and `n/k` form an admissible set of linear size, and the ambient `{1, …, ⌊cn⌋}` bounds it above), so the declaration does not pose the source's open problem, which asks for the exact size and its irregular dependence on `n` and which `erdos_361` already states faithfully.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5446 (open pull request) retypes the answer slot of `erdos_361` so that it can depend on `c`, and its description says `erdos_361.asymptotic` is "deliberately left alone" because its answer is a Θ-class in `n` and may legitimately not depend on `c`; it therefore leaves the triviality of the Θ statement reported here untouched.

title: `higher_full_parts` quantifies over every `ε > 0` instead of some `ε = ε(r, k) > 0`
summary: `Erdos367.erdos_367.variants.higher_full_parts` writes the higher-full-parts extension with `∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →`, which makes the right-hand side trivially false — for r = 3, k = 2, ε = 1 the normalised product is bounded by 2, so its `EReal` limsup is not ⊤ — whereas the intended extension, as discussed on the erdosproblems.com forum thread for 367, asks for some ε = ε(r, k) > 0.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5090 (open pull request) changes this same declaration to `answer(False)` with `category research solved` and links a Lean counterexample at (r, k, ε) = (3, 2, 2); it records the literal `∀ ε > 0` statement as false rather than correcting the quantifier, and its description says it does not settle the corrected `∃ ε > 0` formulation, so the misformalization reported here is not addressed.

title: `sidon_set_lower_bound` states `N.sqrt / 2 ≤ A.card` in ℕ, which is weaker than the advertised √N/2
summary: `Erdos44.sidon_set_lower_bound` asserts the existence of a Sidon set `A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N` with `N.sqrt / 2 ≤ A.card` evaluated entirely in ℕ, so it only demands |A| ≥ ⌊⌊√N⌋/2⌋ rather than the docstring's real bound √N/2: for N = 1 the empty set qualifies and for N = 5 the set {1} does.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5787 (merged pull request) rewrote the neighbouring `Erdos44.greedy_sidon_construction` to conclude `N ≤ A.card ^ 3` and closed our earlier issue #5651; it leaves `Erdos44.sidon_set_lower_bound`'s natural-number `N.sqrt / 2 ≤ A.card` untouched, which is the defect reported here.

title: Coverage statements admit `A = {1}`, and `log_power`'s exponent `c` elaborates as ℕ
summary: `erdos_542.parts.ii`, `erdos_542.variants.schinzel_szekeres` and `erdos_542.variants.log_power` quantify over `IsLcmFree n A` without requiring `1 ∉ A`, so `A = {1}` (for which `uncovered n {1} = ∅`) refutes the lower bound of `parts.ii` already at `n = 1` and proves the two construction statements outright without any Schinzel–Szekeres construction, while in `log_power` the unannotated `c` of `∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ n in atTop, … ≤ n / (log n) ^ c` elaborates as ℕ and so demands `c ≥ 1`, where the source allows an arbitrary real `c > 0`.

title: `erdos_559.variants.rodl_szemeredi` infers the exponent `c` as `ℕ`, so it cannot state the cited `(log n)^(1/60)` bound
summary: In `Erdos559.erdos_559.variants.rodl_szemeredi` the unannotated `∃ c > 0` in `C * n * (log n) ^ c ≤ sizeRamsey G G` elaborates at type `ℕ`, so the statement demands a positive integer logarithmic exponent and is equivalent to its exponent-1 form, whereas the Rödl–Szemerédi bound cited in the docstring and on erdosproblems.com/559 is `n (log n)^c` for a small positive real `c`, identified as `1/60` by Tikhomirov (arXiv:2210.05818) and Draganić–Petrova (arXiv:2207.05048).

title: `erdos_664.variants.block_design` omits the block-size bound `|A i| > c√n` and the parameter `c`
summary: `Erdos664.erdos_664.variants.block_design` asks for one absolute `K` for every family satisfying only the unique-pair-coverage hypothesis, dropping the parameter `c` and the hypothesis `c * √n < (A i).card` that [Er81] §VI keeps (only `c < 1` is meant to be omitted in this variant), so its right-hand side is false for trivial reasons: with n = m = 1 and `A 0 = ∅` the hypothesis holds vacuously but no `B` meets the empty block.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5495 (open pull request) adds its own `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/664.lean` as a new file, predating the merged one, whose single theorem `erdos_664` does keep `0 < c`, `c < 1` and `c * Real.sqrt n < e.card`; it contains no block-design variant, so it does not address the omission reported here.

title: `variants.tao` allows `m = 1`, making Tao's divisor bound `τ(n/m)/m ≤ G n` false
summary: `Erdos673.erdos_673.variants.tao` assumes only `hn : 0 < n` and `hm : m ∣ n`, so `m = 1` is admitted and the asserted `((n / m).divisors.card : ℝ) / m ≤ G n` fails — n = m = 1 gives 1 ≤ G 1 = 0 and n = 2, m = 1 gives 2 ≤ 1/2 — whereas Tao's observation and the file's own cited Lean proof require `1 < m`.

title: `exceptional_count` bounds an index-scale count by `X / (log X) ^ 2`, one log factor too strong
summary: `erdos_682.variants.exceptional_count` counts exceptional indices `n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X` and bounds that count by `(X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ 2`, but Gafni–Tao's `≪ X / (log X)^2` counts gaps whose lower prime satisfies `p_n ∈ [X, 2X]`, which over the first `N` indices yields only `O(N / log N)`, so the Lean statement (and its docstring) is stronger than the cited theorem by a logarithmic factor and is incompatible with the paper's conditional asymptotic `c N / log N` for the index count.

title: `erdos_748.variants.lower_bound` uses natural division in `2 ^ (n / 2)`, weakening the sourced `2^(n/2)` bound
summary: `Erdos748.erdos_748.variants.lower_bound` states `2 ^ (n / 2) ≤ f n` with `n / 2` computed in ℕ, so for odd `n = 2m+1` it requires only `2^m ≤ f n` rather than the `2^(n/2) = 2^m·√2` of the remark on erdosproblems.com/748 that its own docstring quotes (at `n = 1` it asks for `f 1 ≥ 1` instead of `f 1 ≥ √2`), and there is no asymptotic notation or constant here to absorb the rounding.

title: `erdos_772.variants.upper_bound` asserts the `n^{2/3}` bound for all `k ≥ 1`, where it fails at k = 1, 2
summary: `Erdos772.erdos_772.variants.upper_bound` claims `∃ C, ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ n, (H k n : ℝ) ≤ C * n^(2/3)`, but with this file's ordered-pair counting convention the constraint `∀ m, sumRep A m ≤ 2` forces `A` itself to be Sidon, so `H 2 n = n` (and the documented truncation gives `H 1 n = n`), which no fixed real `C` can bound by `C * n^(2/3)`; Erdős's B₂^(2) construction supports the bound only from `k ≥ 4` under that convention.

title: `ncard_add_repr` counts ordered representations and `variants.fixed_ε` uses the endpoint constant `(log(4/3))⁻¹`
summary: `Erdos868.ncard_add_repr` counts arbitrary tuples `a : Fin o → ℕ` with `∑ a i = n`, i.e. ordered representations, while Erdős–Nathanson and Larsen–Larsen count nondecreasing ones (so the Lean count is about twice the source's r_A(n)), and `Erdos868.erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε` hypothesises only `∀ᶠ n, (Real.log (4/3))⁻¹ * Real.log n < f n`, whereas Erdős–Nathanson's Theorem 2 assumes `c * log n < f n` for some fixed `c > (log(4/3))⁻¹`, so the Lean statement asserts the endpoint case with an inflated representation count.

title: `green_37_bigO` and `green_37_littleO` constrain the comparison function not at all, so trivial answers settle them
summary: `Green37.green_37_bigO` and `Green37.green_37_littleO` ask only for some `f` with `(fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] f` resp. `=o[atTop] f` and impose no sharpness requirement, so `answer(fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ))` and `answer(fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ 2)` prove them for every `k` via the elementary cover `{0, …, k*N}` (which gives `m N k ≤ k*N + 1`), although both carry `category research open` and Green's Problem 37 and its comments ask for the smallest cover and the lower bound `F_k(N) ≫_k N^(1-c_k)`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5840 (merged pull request) fixed a different defect in the same file, the answer slots of `green_37`, `green_37_asymptotic` and `green_37_theta` not depending on the binders `N` and `k`; it left `green_37_bigO` and `green_37_littleO` unchanged, so their unrestricted comparison functions (still typed `ℕ → ℝ`, independent of `k`) remain as reported here.

title: `ame_7_exists_iff` is stated for every `d : ℕ`, but `ExistsAME 7 1` holds while `3 ≤ 1` fails
summary: `OpenQuantumProblem35.ame_7_exists_iff (d : ℕ) : ExistsAME 7 d ↔ 3 ≤ d` quantifies over all local dimensions including d = 1, where the file's definitions make `ExistsAME 7 1` true (the unique computational-basis configuration with amplitude 1 has 1×1 maximally mixed reductions) while the right-hand side is false, so the classification is refutable as written; the cited seven-party classification excludes the trivial dimension d = 1.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5561 (merged pull request, 2026-09-17, i.e. before the reviewed commit) introduced `ame_7_exists_iff (d : ℕ) : ExistsAME 7 d ↔ 3 ≤ d` and used it to mark `ame_7_6_open` and `ame_7_10_open` solved; it is the origin of the statement flagged here and imposes no lower bound on `d`, so the d = 1 case is unaddressed.

title: `variants.odd`'s `f.reverse ≠ f` does not exclude antireciprocal `f`, so the golden-ratio bound fails
summary: `LehmerMahlerMeasureProblem.lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.odd` assumes only `f.reverse ≠ f`, which still admits antireciprocal polynomials with `f.reverse = -f`, so `f = X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 + X^3 + X^2 + X - 1` has all odd coefficients and `1 < M(f) ≈ 1.582347 < M(X^2 - X - 1) = (1+√5)/2`, refuting the theorem, whereas the source's nonreciprocity condition (Smyth's survey defines reciprocal by z^d P(1/z) = ±P(z)) excludes both signs.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5734 (merged pull request, 2026-09-13) is what added this `hf' : f.reverse ≠ f` to `variants.odd` (and `Irreducible f` to `variants.not_reciprocal`), closing our earlier issue #5706, which is now closed; it excludes only `f.reverse = f`, not `f.reverse = -f`, so the antireciprocal counterexamples reported here remain.

title: `conjecture141` uses `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ)`, flooring the source's unrounded `girth/2` and losing a vertex at odd girth
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141.conjecture141` states the bound as `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ) - 1 + max_v λ(v) ≤ largestInducedTreeSize G`, where `G.girth / 2` is natural-number division, so for odd girth `2k+1` it asserts only `k - 1 + λ ≤ tree(G)` instead of DeLaViña's unrounded `tree(G) ≥ (1/2)·girth - 1 + max_v λ(v)` (equivalently `⌈girth/2⌉ - 1 + λ`), and the docstring's `⌊girth(G) / 2⌋` repeats the rounding.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4454 (merged pull request, merged 2026-09-21T18:06Z, after the reviewed commit) proves `conjecture141` in-repository and flips it to `category research solved`; its description states that the conjecture statement itself is unchanged, so the floored `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ)` reported here is still present, and sharpening the bound to the unrounded form would require extending that new proof.

title: `conjecture33` uses `distavg`, the mean of nearest-`M` distances, not `dist_avg(M, V)` over nonzero pairs
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture33.conjecture33` bounds `path G` by `⌈2 * distavg G M⌉`, where `distavg` averages over all vertices the minimum distance to `M`, including the zero terms for v ∈ M, whereas WOWII's glossary defines `dist_avg(M, V)` as the average of all nonzero `dist(u, v)` with u ∈ M and v ∈ V; on the perfect binary tree of depth 5 the two quantities are 11/21 and 1797/310, giving the true bound 2 ≤ 11 rather than the false 12 ≤ 11, so the recorded `answer(False)` concerns a different inequality.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5733 (merged pull request) made exactly this correction in the sibling file `GraphConjecture34.lean`, replacing `distavg` by an inline average of the nonzero `G.dist s v` over `S × V`; its description states that `GraphConjecture33` uses `distavg` with the same defect and leaves it 'for a separate issue', so this file is still unfixed.
